title: Rose geranium soy candle
subtitle: A floral container candle for bedrooms and bathrooms
excerpt: A soy container candle scented with rose geranium and bergamot essential oils. A softer, more affordable floral than rose absolute, with a warm, herbal undertone. Makes one 200 ml jar candle.
sourceNotes: Rose geranium essential oil usage in candlemaking: general aromatherapy and candle formulation reference. Essential oil flash points in soy wax: candle safety reference. IFRA guidelines for geranium and bergamot EOs.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~200 ml jar, ~35 burn hours)
recipe.batchNotes: Four or five jars per session.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years unlit in a cool, dark place. Rose geranium essential oil is moderately stable in soy wax; the floral note remains for 12 to 18 months.

glossaryTerms.definition: The lowest temperature at which an essential oil can produce enough vapour to ignite. In candlemaking, fragrance and essential oils should be added below the flash point to prevent flaring. Rose geranium has a flash point of around 75°C; add it at 60°C for safety.

content.text: A floral soy candle for bedrooms and bathrooms. Rose geranium essential oil (Pelargonium roseum) gives a warm rose-and-herb scent that is fresher and less heavy than rose absolute and considerably more affordable. Adding essential oils below the
of the oil prevents volatile flare-up at the pour stage; 60°C is well below rose geranium's flash point.
Never leave a burning candle unattended or near curtains or other flammable materials.

items.prepNote: 2% of wax weight; lifts the floral with a bright citrus note
pre-tabbed cotton wick sized for a 200 ml jar

content.text: Warm the jar in a low oven. Fix the wick centred in the base. Melt the soy wax over a bain-marie. Cool to 60°C. Add both essential oils and stir for one minute. Pour into the jar. Leave overnight to set. Trim the wick to 5 mm. Cure for one week.
On the first burn, allow the wax pool to reach the jar edge fully before extinguishing. Trim the wick to 5 mm before each burn.
Two years unlit in a cool, dark place. The rose geranium scent is strongest for the first 12 months.
